title: Doppelgangers
novel:
The gang had a long-standing game: find your [[doppelganger|doppelganger]] — a stranger who looked exactly like you, who [[resembled|resemble]] you in every detail — somewhere in New York. Each of them believed the city held a [[double|double]].

Marshall had found a [[mustachioed|mustachioed]] man who looked like him. Lily spotted a redhead who could be her twin. Barney saw a [[stripper|stripper]] with his smile. Robin found a [[butch|butch]] woman who shared her jaw.

Only Ted had not found his. He began to think he was the only one without a [[lookalike|lookalike]] in the whole city.

"That's because you're [[irreplaceable|irreplaceable]]," Lily said kindly.

Then, one evening, Ted saw him — a man across the bar with the same face, the same [[gestures|gesture]], the same [[awkward|awkward]] smile. Ted stared. The man stared back, as if [[destiny|destiny]] had played a joke. Then he turned and left.

Marshall and Lily, meanwhile, made a bigger decision. They would start trying for a [[baby|baby]]. The search for doubles was over; the search for a new life had begun. Some [[coincidences|coincidence]], Ted realized, were the universe's way of saying that no one was truly alone — and that every ending was just a [[disguised|disguise]] beginning.

doppelganger.en: someone who looks exactly like you

double.en: someone who looks just like another

stripper.en: a person who removes clothes for money

lookalike.en: a person who closely resembles another

gesture.en: a movement of the body to express something

destiny.en: the things meant to happen to you

coincidence.en: when things happen together by chance
